name: Electric steam cracking
applications: low-carbon ethylene and propylene when power is renewable
principle: The gas-fired radiant coils of a steam cracker are replaced by coils heated with electricity, so the furnace itself emits no combustion CO2. The rest of the plant (quench, compression, cryogenic separation) is unchanged, which makes the route a retrofit option for existing crackers if renewable power and grid capacity are available.

performance.metric: CO2 reduction potential versus conventional cracking
performance.basis: BASF, SABIC and Linde claim at least 90% with renewable power (potential, not measured)

source.note: BASF, SABIC and Linde press release, 17 April 2024

reference_plants.name: BASF Ludwigshafen electric cracking demonstration (BASF, SABIC, Linde)
reference_plants.capacity: two furnaces, about 4 t/h feed, 6 MW renewable power
reference_plants.status: inaugurated 17 April 2024; demonstration continuing, testing two heating concepts; the project won the ICIS Innovation Award 2024 (November 2024) and the Edison Award 2025 (May 2025); Linde is commercialising the technology under the Starbridge brand (as of September 2025)

source.note: BASF sustainability news, eFurnace Edison Award, September 2025 (read 28 October 2026); start-up from BASF, SABIC and Linde press release, 17 April 2024

limitations: Needs very large amounts of renewable electricity
Only a small demonstration so far
